title: New Ramayana Poster Spotlights Yash as Ravana After MrBeast's Mumbai Event
excerpt: The makers released a new official poster of Yash as Ravana — in a gemstone-studded crown and royal regalia — days after a Mumbai pre-release event where MrBeast's viral 'Jai Shri Ram' moment headlined the crossover push ahead of the Diwali 2026 release.
body:
• The makers of Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana have unveiled a new official poster of Yash as Ravana — a heavily embellished gemstone-studded golden crown, layered pearl necklaces and gold bracelets, with the actor's intense expression front and centre.
  • The reveal landed days after a special Mumbai pre-release event attended by YouTube creator MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson), where a clip of him chanting "Jai Shri Ram" alongside Ranbir Kapoor went viral; the event also made headlines for a delay of over three hours that led several journalists to walk out.
  • The two-part epic stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in association with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations.
  • Ramayana: Part 1 releases worldwide on November 6, 2026, timed with Diwali, in IMAX and five Indian languages — Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam — with Part 2 scheduled for Diwali 2027.

The makers of Ramayana have given audiences their sharpest look yet at the film's dark heart, unveiling a new official poster featuring Yash as Ravana in full royal regalia. The visual was released after midnight following a special Mumbai pre-release event attended by MrBeast.

The makers captioned the reveal "The ruler of all 3 worlds, Ravana," framing the film as "Our Truth" and "Our History." Fans praised the scale and aura of the design. Yash's Ravana had already drawn attention in the film's earlier promotional material, but this poster gives the clearest statement yet of how the character has been imagined — a towering mythic force rather than a fleeting tease.

The MrBeast Event That Set It Up

The poster landed days after a high-profile pre-release gathering in Mumbai that brought together Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Ravie Dubey, producer Namit Malhotra, director Nitesh Tiwari and guest Jimmy Donaldson — better known as MrBeast, one of the most-followed YouTube creators in the world.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1zip1rNaNYs

The moment that travelled furthest was a short clip of Ranbir guiding MrBeast to chant "Jai Shri Ram" to the audience, which went viral as the campaign's cross-cultural publicity hook. During the event, Kapoor described Lord Ram as "Maryada Purushottam" — an ideal man who prioritizes duty and sacrifice over personal gain — and said he hoped the film would introduce Indian culture and history to a global audience.

"He is 'Maryada Purushottam' — an ideal man who prioritizes duty and sacrifice over personal gain. I hope this film introduces Indian culture and history to a global audience."

— Ranbir Kapoor, at the Ramayana pre-release event in Mumbai

Producers reiterated the two-part theatrical plan and said localized versions are being prepared for international markets — a push MrBeast's appearance is meant to amplify. The event was not without friction: it ran over three hours late, with reporters staging a walkout and organisers reportedly telling the media they could leave.

Production and Release

Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in association with the Oscar-winning visual effects studio DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations. Yash's involvement goes beyond performance — he is backing the project as a producer, and the poster's commanding Ravana stands in deliberate contrast to the endearing poster of Ranbir, Sai Pallavi and Ravie Dubey as Ram, Sita and Lakshman released alongside it.

Ramayana: Part 1 releases worldwide on November 6, 2026, timed with Diwali, in IMAX and five Indian languages — Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam — with Part 2 scheduled for Diwali 2027. For Yash, the film is one of his last confirmed major features after 2022's K.G.F: Chapter 2, the blockbuster that cemented his pan-India stardom; he has kept his slate highly selective since.

What It Signals

The strategy is clear: Ramayana is being sold as a prestige spectacle for worldwide audiences, with the makers leaning on scale, star power and global pop-culture crossovers to reach beyond the traditional Hindi-film market. The poster strategy is disciplined too — the Ram-Sita-Lakshman visual established the emotional core, and the new Ravana poster establishes the threat, giving Part 1 a defined antagonist and Yash billing commensurate with his draw.

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, Ramayana is shaping into the kind of event release that plays well outside India: a worldwide IMAX rollout, five Indian languages, and explicitly localized versions for international markets. The MrBeast crossover is the clearest signal yet that the producers are courting global audiences — including the Indian families abroad who prefer big Indian releases on the big screen.

What's Next

The next milestones are the second trailer and advance-booking announcements, plus details on the scale of the international release. Beyond that, Part 2 is already on the calendar for Diwali 2027, making this a two-year theatrical bet for the producers.
